day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect to your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort, check in, and freshen up. Take a short stroll around the neighborhood to get oriented. Pick up snacks or a late-night slice of pizza al taglio from a nearby 24-hour bakery or convenience store.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night pizza al taglio or a panino from a nearby alimentari or 24-hour spot near the hotel (€3–6)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for tomorrow. Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass (€32–€52) online in advance for free/discounted museum entry and unlimited public transport. Validate your transit card as soon as you board any bus or metro.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a classic Roman breakfast at a local bar — espresso and a cornetto (€2–3). Then head to the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (pre-booked ticket recommended, ~€20). Arrive early (opening is 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vast collections, Egyptian antiquities, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican Museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica for free — the climb to the dome costs only €8 and offers panoramic views of Rome. Grab lunch at a nearby trattoria on Via della Conciliazione or grab street food from a market stall (€5–8). Walk across the Tiber via Ponte Sant'Angelo and explore the charming Prati neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Piazza Navona and the historic centro storico. Visit the stunning Pantheon (free entry in the evening after 19:00 or €5 during the day). Enjoy aperitivo hour — many bars offer free snacks with a €5–7 drink. End the evening with a budget-friendly dinner in Trastevere.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pizza al taglio or a tramezzino sandwich near the Vatican (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Trastevere — cacio e pepe or amatriciana pasta (€10–14 per person). Try Trattoria da Enzo al 29 or similar local spots.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets online in advance to skip the long queues. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for St. Peter's Basilica and the Vatican. Carry a reusable water bottle — Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Borghese Gallery Art Tour (pre-booking mandatory, timed entry every 2 hours, ~€15–20 + €2 booking fee). Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic masterpieces. The gallery limits visitors to 360 per session, making it an intimate and unhurried experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a picnic lunch in the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — buy supplies from a nearby alimentari or market (€5–8). Rent a rowboat on the small lake (€3–5) or simply relax among the umbrella pines. In the afternoon, walk down the Spanish Steps (Trinità dei Monti) and window-shop along Via Condotti without spending a euro.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Campo de' Fiori market area (market is mornings only, but the piazza is vibrant at night). Grab a gelato from a reputable gelateria — look for 'artigianale' signs (€2.50–4). Dinner near the Jewish Ghetto area, which offers some of Rome's most authentic and affordable trattorias.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fruit, and coffee at a local bar or grab a brioche (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese — fresh bread, local cheese, prosciutto, and fruit from a nearby market (€6–9)
meals.dinner: Cacio e pepe or Jewish-style artichokes (carciofi alla giudia) at a trattoria near the Jewish Ghetto (€10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online as soon as possible at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery only allows 2-hour visits, so plan accordingly. Villa Borghese is free to enter and a perfect midday retreat from the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Ancient Rome & Palatine Hill Guided Tour (€25–35 with a licensed guide). Walk through the Roman Forum's ancient temples and triumphal arches, climb Palatine Hill for sweeping panoramic views over the city, and explore the iconic Colosseum. A single combined ticket (€16) covers the Forum, Palatine Hill, and Colosseum — the guided tour adds context and skips queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore the Circus Maximus (free, outdoor) and the nearby Aventine Hill. Visit the famous Knights of Malta Keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) — peer through the keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, completely free. Stroll through the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for more city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic food district. Explore the covered Testaccio Market (closes by 14:00, so plan an early evening walk around the neighborhood). Dinner in Testaccio, famous for traditional Roman offal dishes and hearty cucina povera — perfect for food lovers on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Cornetto and cappuccino at a bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Supplì (fried rice balls) or a porchetta sandwich from a street vendor near the Forum area (€4–7)
meals.dinner: Traditional Roman dinner in Testaccio — rigatoni con pajata or coda alla vaccinara at a local trattoria (€10–14 per person). Try Flavio al Velavevodetto or similar.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Colosseum/Forum tickets online in advance at coopculture.it to avoid 1–2 hour queues, especially in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–7 km on cobblestones. Bring sunscreen and a hat as the Forum and Palatine Hill are very exposed to the sun.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Capitoline Museums (€15, the world's oldest public museums) on Capitoline Hill — home to the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, Caravaggio paintings, and the famous Capitoline Wolf sculpture. The rooftop terrace offers a stunning free view over the Roman Forum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Trevi Fountain (free) and toss a coin for good luck. Explore the charming backstreets of the Tridente neighborhood. Visit the free Palazzo Altemps (part of the National Roman Museum, €10 or covered by Roma Pass) for more ancient sculpture collections. Stop at the historic Mercato di Via della Pace or a local alimentari for an afternoon snack.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Rome's vibrant aperitivo scene — many bars in Pigneto or Prati offer free cicchetti (snacks) with a drink (€5–7). Explore the lively Pigneto neighborhood, Rome's bohemian quarter, for affordable dinner options and a glimpse of local life away from tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Maritozzo (cream-filled bun) and espresso at a traditional Roman bar (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Falafel or a kebab wrap in the area near the Pantheon — Rome has excellent Middle Eastern street food (€5–7). Or try a classic Roman supplì.
meals.dinner: Osteria or trattoria in Pigneto neighborhood — pasta and house wine (€10–13 per person). Look for the 'menu del giorno' (daily set menu) for the best value.

day_by_day.notes: The Trevi Fountain is most magical at night when lit up — consider returning after dinner for photos. Friday evenings in Pigneto are lively with locals. If you have a Roma Pass, use it for Capitoline Museums entry to maximize savings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Piazza Campo de' Fiori morning market (7:00–14:00) — one of Rome's most colorful open-air markets selling fresh produce, spices, flowers, and local specialties. Sample free tastings from vendors and stock up on picnic supplies. Nearby, explore the Palazzo Farnese exterior (free) and the charming streets of the Renaissance quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided walking tour of Rome's lesser-known art churches — Santa Maria sopra Minerva (Rome's only Gothic church, with Michelangelo's Christ the Redeemer statue), San Luigi dei Francesi (three Caravaggio masterpieces, free), and Sant'Agostino (another Caravaggio). These are completely free and house world-class art. Finish with a gelato break.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Trastevere for your final evening in this neighborhood — the cobblestone streets are magical on Saturday nights. Browse the weekend flea market atmosphere near Porta Portese (daytime Sundays, but the area is lively Saturday evening). Enjoy a leisurely farewell dinner with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Freshly squeezed orange juice and a pastry from Campo de' Fiori market vendors (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic assembled from Campo de' Fiori market — olives, cheese, bread, and seasonal fruit on a bench near the Tiber (€7–10)
meals.dinner: Trastevere trattoria — cacio e pepe, tiramisu, and a carafe of house wine (€14–18 per person). Try Tonnarello or Da Enzo al 29.

day_by_day.notes: San Luigi dei Francesi requires a €0.50 coin to illuminate the Caravaggio paintings — bring small change. Saturday in Trastevere is very crowded by 20:00, so arrive for dinner by 19:00 or make a reservation. The Caravaggios in these free churches rival anything in paid museums.

day_by_day.morning: Sunday morning in Rome is magical — visit Porta Portese Flea Market (7:00–14:00), one of Europe's largest and most famous flea markets. Browse thousands of stalls selling antiques, vintage clothing, books, and curiosities along the Tiber. It's free to enter and a fantastic cultural experience. Pick up affordable souvenirs — local ceramics, vintage prints, or artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a final afternoon at the MAXXI – National Museum of 21st Century Arts (€12, reduced €9) or the free Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna for modern and contemporary Italian art. Alternatively, take a relaxing walk along the Lungotevere (Tiber riverbank), stopping at Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior free, interior €15) for photos. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Roman dinner near the hotel or in a central neighborhood. Splurge slightly on your last meal — try a classic Roman carbonara with guanciale (not bacon!) at a reliable trattoria. Head to the airport via Leonardo Express from Roma Termini or arrange a pre-booked transfer.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a warm cornetto at a local bar — a perfect final Roman breakfast (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Porchetta sandwich or pizza bianca from a Porta Portese vendor or nearby forno (bakery) (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Final Roman dinner — authentic carbonara, cacio e pepe, or gricia pasta with a glass of local Frascati wine (€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is cash-only and very crowded — keep valuables secure and arrive by 8:00 AM for the best finds. If departing on June 21, confirm your flight time and allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in. The Leonardo Express runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes to Fiumicino Airport (€14).

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (30 min, ~€14), then taxi or rideshare to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack near the hotel — look for a open pizzeria al taglio or a 24h bar for a quick panino and a glass of wine to wind down

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll need energy for the week ahead. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since arrival is late night. Pack light snacks in your carry-on in case options near the hotel are limited at that hour.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely Italian breakfast at a nearby café — espresso, cornetto, and fresh orange juice. Stroll around the neighborhood to get your bearings and pick up any essentials.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Borghese Gallery Art Tour. Book a timed-entry slot in advance (entry is strictly limited to 2-hour windows). Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures including Apollo and Daphne, and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. The gallery sits within the lush Villa Borghese park — take a relaxed walk through the gardens afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk. Wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì, cacio e pepe, artichokes alla romana, and local wines. This is a perfect introduction to Roman street food culture and a great way to meet fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Café Sant'Eustachio or a local bar near the hotel — espresso and cornetto (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Casual trattoria near Villa Borghese — try pasta alla gricia or a simple antipasto plate (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Walk; supplement with a sit-down dessert at a gelateria in Trastevere (~€4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance booking — secure tickets as soon as possible as they sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the evening food tour. The Trastevere neighborhood is lively and safe at night.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel. Book a skip-the-line or early-bird entry (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vast collection — Egyptian antiquities, Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms — culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) right next door. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views over Rome (~€8 with elevator). Afterward, stroll across the Tiber via Castel Sant'Angelo and explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Prati neighborhood near the Vatican — a local favorite away from tourist traps. Enjoy a relaxed Roman dinner and an after-dinner gelato walk.

meals.breakfast: Quick café stop near the hotel before heading out — espresso and a pastry (~€4)
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci in Prati — Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio, sold by weight. Inventive toppings, exceptional quality (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzeria Ristorante in Prati — try cacio e pepe, saltimbocca alla romana, and a carafe of house wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are extremely crowded in summer — early entry or guided skip-the-line tickets are strongly recommended. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) to enter the Basilica and Sistine Chapel. Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class. Arrive at the vibrant open-air market by 9:00 AM to select fresh seasonal produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and herbs with your instructor. Then head to a nearby kitchen for a hands-on cooking class — learn to make fresh pasta, a classic Roman sauce, and a traditional dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (which typically includes lunch from what you've made), take a leisurely afternoon to explore the surrounding neighborhood. Visit Piazza Navona with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, then wander to the Pantheon (book timed entry online, ~€5).
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour in the historic center — many bars offer free snacks with a Aperol Spritz or Negroni (~€8–12). Then enjoy a light dinner or street food along the way back.

meals.breakfast: Snack at the Campo de' Fiori market — fresh fruit, a slice of focaccia, or a supplì (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Osteria del Pegno near Piazza Navona — intimate, mid-range Roman cuisine with seasonal specials (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market runs Monday–Saturday mornings until about 2:00 PM. Book the cooking class in advance. The Pantheon now requires a timed ticket — purchase online to avoid queues. Afternoon is a good time to visit as morning crowds thin out.

day_by_day.morning: Ancient Rome & Palatine Hill Guided Tour. Join a guided tour of the Roman Forum, Palatine Hill, and the Colosseum. Walk in the footsteps of emperors and senators, enjoy panoramic views of the ancient city from Palatine Hill, and get expert historical context that brings the ruins to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore the Circus Maximus and the Aventine Hill neighborhood. Visit the famous Knights of Malta keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, and the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Testaccio — Rome's traditional working-class food neighborhood. Explore the Testaccio Market (if still open) or browse the lively streets. This is the best neighborhood for authentic Roman cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Bar near the hotel or close to the Colosseum area — espresso and cornetto (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Forum area — a packed sandwich from a nearby alimentari or a casual café (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — beloved local trattoria famous for Roman classics like rigatoni con pajata or coda alla vaccinara (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Colosseum and Roman Forum require advance booking — combined tickets sell out fast in summer. The guided tour typically lasts 3–4 hours, so wear sunscreen and a hat as there is limited shade. Testaccio is a 20-minute walk or short bus ride from the Colosseum area.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for personal exploration or revisiting a favorite spot. Consider visiting the Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums, with stunning ancient Roman sculptures and a rooftop terrace view of the Forum) or browsing the antique shops along Via dei Coronari.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Ghetto and Largo di Torre Argentina (where Julius Caesar was assassinated — now a cat sanctuary and archaeological site, free to visit). Take a slow walk along the Tiber riverbanks. Stop at a local pasticceria for a mid-afternoon treat — try a maritozzo (cream-filled Roman bun).
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate your penultimate night. Head to a well-regarded restaurant in the Pigneto or Monti neighborhoods for a more refined Roman dining experience with natural wines.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel — take your time (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Forno Campo de' Fiori — excellent pizza bianca, focaccia, and baked goods for a casual lunch on the go (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Monti — beloved neighborhood gem specializing in cuisine from the Marche region with Roman influences; reservations recommended (~€40–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Capitoline Museums are closed on Mondays — check the day of the week before planning. Largo di Torre Argentina is free and the cat sanctuary is a quirky, charming stop. Monti is one of Rome's hippest neighborhoods and great for an evening stroll before or after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final Roman morning — wake up early and take one last espresso at a neighborhood bar standing at the counter, Italian-style. Do any remaining souvenir shopping (artisan shops in Trastevere or Monti are better value than tourist stalls). Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch. Take a last stroll past a beloved spot — toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain for good luck and a guaranteed return to Rome. Head to the airport (allow 1.5–2 hours including transit).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome. Buon viaggio!

meals.breakfast: Standing espresso and cornetto at a local bar — the most Roman way to end the trip (~€2–4)
meals.lunch: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere for a final classic Roman lunch — cacio e pepe, carciofi, tiramisu (~€25–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and factor in travel time to the airport — Fiumicino is about 45–60 minutes from central Rome by Leonardo Express. Leave extra buffer time in summer due to airport congestion. Keep some euros handy for tips, last-minute snacks, and airport expenses.

day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore the elegant streets of the historic center at your own pace. Visit the stunning Piazza Navona (Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers) and the Pantheon — one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Consider a private guide for the Pantheon to unlock its architectural secrets. Browse high-end boutiques along Via Condotti or Via del Babuino.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar — Il Sorpasso Rooftop or Hotel de la Ville's Cielo Rooftop Bar offers sweeping views over the Roman rooftops. Then a private dinner reservation at Imàgo at Hotel Hassler (panoramic terrace, contemporary Italian fine dining with views of the Spanish Steps).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class labor — a sit-down meal of the dishes you prepared, paired with local wines selected by your instructor
meals.dinner: Imàgo Restaurant at Hotel Hassler — tasting menu with sommelier-led wine pairing; reserve the terrace table for sunset views over Rome

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and Imàgo well in advance — both are highly sought after. Wear comfortable shoes for the market and afternoon walking. The Pantheon now requires a small entry fee; pre-book online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — private early-access tour beginning at 8:00 AM before general public entry. Your expert private guide leads you through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel in relative tranquility. Conclude with a visit to St. Peter's Basilica and, if available, ascend to the dome for panoramic city views. (~3.5 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Castel Sant'Angelo (Hadrian's Mausoleum) — a short walk from the Vatican. Climb to the top for spectacular views over the Tiber and St. Peter's. Afterwards, stroll across the Ponte Sant'Angelo lined with Bernini's angel sculptures. Relax with a gelato from Gelateria dei Gracchi (one of Rome's finest artisanal gelaterias nearby).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the terrace at Settimio all'Arancio, followed by dinner at Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio or Il Convivio Troiani (3 Michelin stars) — one of Rome's most prestigious fine dining experiences, offering refined Roman cuisine in an intimate 16th-century palazzo setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — early and light, given the 8:00 AM Vatican start
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Il Sorpasso or a curated picnic of premium Roman deli items (prosciutto di Parma, aged pecorino, focaccia, truffle products) from Roscioli Salumeria near Campo de' Fiori
meals.dinner: Il Convivio Troiani — chef's tasting menu with optional wine pairing; one of Rome's most celebrated fine dining destinations

day_by_day.notes: Early Vatican access is essential — book the private early-entry tour months in advance. Dress code for St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees. Il Convivio Troiani is intimate (small room), so confirm reservation well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Ancient Rome & Palatine Hill Guided Tour — private expert guide leads you through the Roman Forum, up Palatine Hill (where emperors once lived) for sweeping panoramic views over the ancient city, and into the Colosseum with skip-the-line access. Optional: underground Colosseum arena floor access for an exclusive perspective. (~4 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, refresh at a nearby wine bar — Cavour 313, a beloved enoteca steps from the Forum. Then head to the Aventine Hill neighborhood: visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (perfectly framing St. Peter's dome) and the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for a relaxing afternoon with panoramic views. Browse artisan shops in the Testaccio neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Testaccio — Rome's authentic culinary heartland. Reserve at Flavio al Velavevodetto, a beloved institution set into Monte Testaccio (a hill made of ancient Roman amphora shards), serving robust traditional Roman cuisine: rigatoni alla pajata, coda alla vaccinara, and abbacchio al forno.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Wine and charcuterie at Cavour 313 enoteca — exceptional wine list, artisanal cheeses, and cured meats in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto, Testaccio — traditional Roman feast; pair with a robust Cesanese del Piglio or Montepulciano d'Abruzzo

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum arena floor access separately — limited spots. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the Forum and Palatine Hill (uneven ancient paving). The Aventine Keyhole has a small queue; visit mid-afternoon to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury leisure morning — sleep in and enjoy a long breakfast at the resort. Optional: book a 90-minute resort spa treatment (deep tissue massage or Roman thermal ritual). Alternatively, arrange a private art studio visit or a bespoke jewelry workshop in the historic center — many Roman artisans offer exclusive private sessions for luxury travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Doria Pamphilj Gallery — one of Rome's best-kept secrets, a private palazzo gallery still owned by the noble Doria Pamphilj family, housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X, Caravaggio originals, and Bernini busts. Audio guide narrated by a family member adds a uniquely personal touch. Afterwards, wander the elegant Via Veneto (immortalized in Fellini's La Dolce Vita) for luxury shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private rooftop dining experience — arrange a private chef's table dinner on a panoramic Rome rooftop through the resort's concierge. Alternatively, dine at La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri (the only 3-Michelin-star restaurant in Rome) — chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu with views over the eternal city is the pinnacle of Roman fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — request a private terrace setup with fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and Champagne if desired
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Fortunato al Pantheon — a Roman institution since 1975, beloved by politicians and artists; excellent cacio e pepe and abbacchio
meals.dinner: La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri — 3-Michelin-star tasting menu (book months in advance); request the window table for unparalleled city views at sunset

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Roman dining — reservations open months ahead and fill instantly. Smart formal attire required. The Doria Pamphilj Gallery is closed Thursdays; verify opening days before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Final Roman morning — wake early for a sunrise walk or private photography tour of the Spanish Steps, Trevi Fountain, and Pantheon before the crowds arrive. Toss your coin in the Trevi Fountain (tradition says you'll return to Rome). Return to the resort for a farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: last-minute luxury shopping along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi, Gucci flagship stores) or a final gelato and espresso ritual at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè — Rome's most celebrated coffee institution. Pack, check out, and arrange private luxury transfer to Fiumicino Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome. If flight is evening or next day, arrange late check-out with the resort and spend the afternoon at the resort spa or pool.

meals.breakfast: Farewell resort breakfast — request a special send-off spread on the terrace
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Ristorante Roscioli — Rome's legendary deli-restaurant hybrid; order the carbonara (considered among the city's best) and a glass of natural wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board, depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Fiumicino Airport. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Ask the resort concierge to arrange any last-minute gift wrapping for artisan purchases. Sant'Eustachio serves espresso with pre-sweetened sugar — specify 'amaro' if you prefer it unsweetened.
